title: Founding Flipkart as an Amazon-style bookstore
statement: Two ex-Amazon Bangalore engineers quit to start an Indian e-commerce company with book sales, coding the site themselves and personally delivering early orders.
outcome: Flipkart pioneered Indian e-commerce — cash on delivery, the Big Billion Days sale — and defined the category until its $16 billion sale to Walmart in 2018.

title: Cash on delivery — inventing trust for Indian e-commerce
statement: The brothers recognized that Indian consumers would not prepay online, and built the COD logistics chain that solved the market's core trust problem.
outcome: COD became the industry's default and unlocked the Indian e-commerce market; it remains the structural difference from Western online retail economics.

title: Myntra acquisition and the app-only controversy
statement: Flipkart bought fashion marketplace Myntra for roughly $300 million, then briefly forced an app-only website shutdown that misread customer behavior.
outcome: Myntra became the profitable core of Flipkart Fashion; the app-only retreat was reversed within months and remains the canonical Indian caution against copying China's playbook.
